keywords.def: a system in which success is determined by a person’s effort and ability
the process of moving to a higher social or economic position than where you started in life
the decline of industrial and manufacturing activity in a country or region
employment that is unstable, insecure, or poorly paid.
an unfair gap between different groups in terms of wealth, opportunity, or power
not growing or improving; remaining at the same level over time
a longing for the past, often based on an idealised or simplified memory

sentences.en: If you work hard, can you build yourself a better life?
sentences.zh: 如果你努力工作，你能为自己创造更好的生活吗？

sentences.en: For a long time, millions of people believed the answer in the USA was yes.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，美国有数百万人坚信答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: The “American Dream” is the idea that anyone, no matter where they start in life, can achieve success through hard work and determination.
sentences.zh: “美国梦”指的是这样一种理念：无论出身如何，任何人都能通过努力工作和坚定信念取得成功。

sentences.en: You could own a home, have a stable job, raise a family, and earn more than your parents.
sentences.zh: 你可以拥有自己的房子、稳定的工作、养育家庭，并且赚得比父母更多。

sentences.en: But today, many people in the US are questioning whether that dream still exists.
sentences.zh: 但如今，许多美国人正在质疑这个梦想是否依然存在。

sentences.en: Housing prices are rising. Student debt is growing.
sentences.zh: 房价在上涨，学生债务在增加。

sentences.en: Many young people feel locked out of the middle class.
sentences.zh: 许多年轻人感到被排挤在中产阶级之外。

sentences.en: Some people argue the American Dream is dead.
sentences.zh: 有人认为美国梦已经破灭。

sentences.en: Hard work no longer guarantees success. Others disagree.
sentences.zh: 努力工作不再是成功的保证，但也有人持不同意见。

sentences.en: They believe America still offers more opportunity than almost anywhere else in the world.
sentences.zh: 他们坚信，与世界上几乎其他任何地方相比，美国依然提供了更多的机遇。

sentences.en: So, what exactly is the American Dream? Where did the idea come from?
sentences.zh: 那么，究竟什么是美国梦？这个理念从何而来？

sentences.en: Why are people losing faith in it? And is it dead or changing?
sentences.zh: 为什么人们对它失去了信心？它究竟是消亡了还是在发生变化？

sentences.en: The American Dream is the belief that anyone in the USA can improve their life through hard work, determination, and opportunity.
sentences.zh: 美国梦是指坚信在美国的任何人都可以通过努力工作、坚定信念和机遇来改善自己的生活。

sentences.en: It doesn’t matter where you were born, whether you are an immigrant or not, how poor or how rich your family is, if you work hard enough, you can build a successful and comfortable life.
sentences.zh: 无论你出生在哪里、是否是移民、家庭是贫穷还是富有，只要你足够努力，就能创造成功而舒适的生活。

sentences.en: For many people in the US, the American Dream is connected to things like building wealth, owning a home, raising your family, and having more opportunities or a better life than your parents.
sentences.zh: 对许多美国人来说，美国梦与积累财富、拥有住房、养育家庭，以及拥有比父母更多的机遇或更好的生活等事情息息相关。

sentences.en: It’s linked to the idea of upward social mobility.
sentences.zh: 它与纵向社会流动的概念紧密相连。

sentences.en: Moving to a higher social or economic position than where you started.
sentences.zh: 即晋升到比你起点更高的社会或经济地位。

sentences.en: You want to have a bigger house, a nicer car, a more luxurious life than your parents.
sentences.zh: 你希望拥有比父母更大的房子、更好的车子以及更奢华的生活。

sentences.en: There are a few key parts to this idea. One is equal opportunity.
sentences.zh: 这个理念包含几个关键部分，其中之一就是机会平等。

sentences.en: Everyone in the American Dream has the same chance to succeed.
sentences.zh: 在мерикан梦中，每个人都有获得成功的同等机会。

sentences.en: Another is meritocracy. Meritocracy is the idea that effort and ability should be what decides whether you’re successful or not.
sentences.zh: 另一个是精英统治，即精英统治是指应该由努力和能力来决定你是否成功。

sentences.en: It shouldn’t be your family or your social class.
sentences.zh: 它不应该取决于你的家庭或社会阶层。

sentences.en: Financial stability is another part of the American Dream, and so is the hope that your children will have a better future than you.
sentences.zh: 财务稳定是美国梦的另一个组成部分，孩子们能拥有比你更好的未来也是一种期望。

sentences.en: Importantly though, we have to mention that the American Dream wasn’t always available to everyone.
sentences.zh: 不过重要的是，我们必须指出，美国梦并非从一开始就对所有人开放。

sentences.en: Many groups have faced major discrimination in the USA in the past, and today as well.
sentences.zh: 在过去以及今天，许多群体都在美国遭遇过严重的歧视。

sentences.en: Black Americans experienced slavery, segregation, and racism.
sentences.zh: 黑人美国人经历过奴隶制、种族隔离和种族主义。

sentences.en: Native Americans were violently removed from their land.
sentences.zh: 美洲原住民被暴力驱逐出他们的土地。

sentences.en: For a long time, women had limited legal and economic rights, and many immigrants and poorer communities struggled to get some of the opportunities that wealthier Americans could get.
sentences.zh: 长期以来，女性的法律和经济权利受到限制，许多移民和贫困社区也很难获得富裕美国人所能得到的机遇。

sentences.en: But, this idea of the American Dream has been a major part of the culture in the USA for the past hundred years or so, maybe longer.
sentences.zh: 但是，在过去的一百年左右甚至更长的时间里，美国梦这一理念一直是美国文化的核心部分。

sentences.en: Actually, where did the idea come from? Well, the US has been seen as a “land of opportunity” for quite a long time.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这个理念源自何处？长期以来，美国一直被视为“机会之地”。

sentences.en: It was seen as a place where you could go and succeed.
sentences.zh: 它被视为一个你可以去闯荡并取得成功的地方。

sentences.en: Compared to the class systems of countries like Britain or France or the poverty of other parts of Europe, the United States seemed like a place where normal people could build a life.
sentences.zh: 与英国、法国等国的阶级制度或欧洲其他地区的贫困相比，美国似乎是一个普通人能够开创生活的地方。

sentences.en: Normal people could own some land and improve their lives.
sentences.zh: 普通人可以拥有一些土地并改善他们的生活。

sentences.en: And this is why so many European immigrants moved to the US in the 18th and 19th centuries.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在18和19世纪有如此多的欧洲移民搬到美国。

sentences.en: The actual phrase “American Dream” became popular in 1931, thanks to the historian James Truslow Adams in his book, The Epic of America.
sentences.zh: “美国梦”这个确切的短语在1931年流行起来，这要归功于历史学家詹姆斯·特鲁斯洛·亚当斯在他的著作《美国史诗》中的阐述。

sentences.en: Adams said the American Dream was not simply about becoming rich.
sentences.zh: 亚当斯表示，美国梦不仅仅是变得富有。

sentences.en: He described it as a society where every person could achieve their full potential and be recognized for their abilities.
sentences.zh: 他将其描述为一个让每个人都能发挥全部潜能并因其能力而得到认可的社会。

sentences.en: Doesn’t matter where you’re born or how you were born, whether you were born rich or poor, if you had potential and ability, you could achieve success.
sentences.zh: 无论你出生在哪里、如何出生，无论你出身贫寒还是富贵，只要你有潜力和能力，你就能取得成功。

sentences.en: I think the American Dream reached its peak after World War II.
sentences.zh: 我认为美国梦在二战后达到了巅峰。

sentences.en: After World War II, the US economy grew rapidly.
sentences.zh: 二战结束后，美国经济迅猛增长。

sentences.en: Manufacturing jobs were strong, wages were increasing, houses were quite affordable.
sentences.zh: 制造业工作岗位充足，工资在上涨，房屋也相当便宜。

sentences.en: Millions of veterans of World War II, so people who had fought for the USA in the war, benefited from the GI Bill.
sentences.zh: 数百万二战退伍军人（即在战争中为美国作战的人）受益于《退伍军人权利法案》。

sentences.en: The GI Bill allowed veterans, former soldiers, to attend university for free or buy homes with cheap mortgages.
sentences.zh: 《退伍军人权利法案》允许退伍老兵（即前士兵）免费上大学或通过低息抵押贷款买房。

sentences.en: This period created the image of the American Dream: a house in the suburbs, a car, a job that’s stable.
sentences.zh: 这段时期塑造了美国梦的经典形象：郊区的房子、一辆车、一份稳定的工作。

sentences.en: Enough money for one income to support your entire family.
sentences.zh: 一个人的收入就足以养活全家人。

sentences.en: You could have one parent working, one parent staying home looking after the children, and have three or four children, and be able to afford that.
sentences.zh: 你可以有一个父母工作，另一个父母在家照顾孩子，养三四个孩子，并且能够负担得起这一切。

sentences.en: Higher education became a lot more accessible after World War II.
sentences.zh: 二战后，高等教育变得更加触手可及。

sentences.en: And many people in the US believed that their children would have better lives in the future.
sentences.zh: 许多美国人坚信，他们的孩子未来会过上更好的生活。

sentences.en: But perhaps this is no longer true. I think a lot of people are now questioning whether their children’s lives will actually be better than their lives.
sentences.zh: 但或许这已经不再是事实。我认为许多人现在都在质疑，他们孩子的未来生活是否真的会比他们自己更好。

sentences.en: And this is not just happening in the US, it’s an issue, a question, that’s happening in a lot of countries.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅发生在美国，这也是许多国家正在面临的一个议题和疑问。

sentences.en: I know in my home country, the UK, a lot of people are questioning, will our lives get better in the future?
sentences.zh: 我知道在我的祖国英国，许多人都在质疑：我们的未来会变得更好吗？

sentences.en: But going back to the USA, it has been suggested that the American Dream is dying… maybe it’s already dead.
sentences.zh: 但回到美国，有人指出美国梦正在消亡……也许它已经死了。

sentences.en: Why? One major reason is rising living costs.
sentences.zh: 为什么？一个主要原因就是生活成本不断上涨。

sentences.en: Across much of the United States, housing prices have increased faster than wages.
sentences.zh: 在全美的大部分地区，房价上涨的速度已经超过了工资上涨的速度。

sentences.en: For most of the 20th century, the average house price was around 3 or 4 times more than the average annual wage.
sentences.zh: 在整个20世纪的大部分时间里，平均房价大约是平均年薪的3到4倍。

sentences.en: Now, it is over 7 times more in quite a lot of places in the US.
sentences.zh: 而现在，在美国相当多的地方，这一数字已经超过了7倍。

sentences.en: Rent has also become incredibly expensive in many cities in the US.
sentences.zh: 在美国的许多城市，租金也变得高得离谱。

sentences.en: I think the average across the country is $2,000 US dollars a month, which is expensive.
sentences.zh: 我认为全国的平均租金是每月2000美元，这真的很贵。

sentences.en: Healthcare costs are famous, or infamous I should say.
sentences.zh: 医疗成本可以说是“声名狼藉”或者说臭名昭著。

sentences.en: If you know anything about the US, you know that healthcare can be really expensive there.
sentences.zh: 如果你对美国有所了解，你就会知道那里的医疗费用可能会非常昂贵。

sentences.en: Childcare is unaffordable for families, and student debt has grown massively.
sentences.zh: 育儿费用对家庭来说难以承受，而且学生债务也大幅飙升。

sentences.en: People are taking out big loans to attend university.
sentences.zh: 人们为了上大学背负了巨额贷款。

sentences.en: I was actually shocked by the childcare costs in the US when I was researching this episode.
sentences.zh: 在研究这一期节目时，我其实对美国的托儿费用感到震惊。

sentences.en: It’s incredible how expensive childcare is.
sentences.zh: 育儿成本高得惊人。

sentences.en: From searching online, it seems like the average is around $1,500 per month per child.
sentences.zh: 从网上的搜索结果来看，每个孩子每月的平均费用似乎在1500美元左右。

sentences.en: So if you have two children younger than school age but you need to work full time, you could be paying $3,000 a month just on childcare.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有两个学龄前儿童，但你需要全职工作，你可能仅在托儿费上就要支付每月3000美元。

sentences.en: Then add $2,000 a month on rent. Many people in the US look at their grandparents, who were able to buy a house in their 20s with a normal job, and then compare that to people today who work full time but can’t really afford rent.
sentences.zh: 再加上每月2000美元的房租。美国的许多人看着他们的祖父母，后者在20多岁时凭一份普通工作就能买得起房，然后将他们与如今全职工作却根本租不起房的现代人进行对比。

sentences.en: Another major issue that’s damaging the American Dream is inequality.
sentences.zh: 另一个正在破坏美国梦的重大问题是不平等。

sentences.en: More and more wealth has become concentrated, owned by, the richest people.
sentences.zh: 越来越多的财富被最富有的人集中和拥有。

sentences.en: But for many ordinary workers, wages are relatively stagnant, especially when you adjust it for inflation.
sentences.zh: 但对许多普通工人来说，工资相对停滞不前，特别是当你根据通货膨胀进行调整时。

sentences.en: There’s also been a major change in the job market around the world, but especially in the USA.
sentences.zh: 全球范围内，劳动力市场也发生了重大变化，美国尤其明显。

sentences.en: During the 20th century, millions of people in the US worked in blue-collar jobs.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪，数百万美国人从事着蓝领工作。

sentences.en: They did things like factory working, or mining, manufacturing.
sentences.zh: 他们从事工厂工作、采矿或制造业等工作。

sentences.en: These were manual industries that paid enough to support a middle-class lifestyle.
sentences.zh: 这些体力劳动行业支付的薪水足以支撑中产阶级的生活方式。

sentences.en: But deindustrialization and outsourcing has moved many of these jobs to other countries, or replaced these jobs with machines.
sentences.zh: 但去工业化和外包将许多这类工作转移到了其他国家，或者被机器所取代。

sentences.en: Many people now work in what economists call “precarious work “.
sentences.zh: 许多人现在从事经济学家所说的“不安全工作”。

sentences.en: Precarious work means jobs that are unstable or insecure.
sentences.zh: 不安全工作意味着不稳定或缺乏保障的工作。

sentences.en: Think about things like the gig economy, delivering food for Uber Eats as an example, or short-term contracts and low-paid service jobs.
sentences.zh: 想想零工经济，比如为Uber Eats送外卖，或者是短期合同和低薪服务业工作。

sentences.en: Many researchers also argue that social mobility has slowed down.
sentences.zh: 许多研究人员还认为，社会流动性已经放缓。

sentences.en: In theory, the American Dream says anyone can rise through society regardless of where you come from.
sentences.zh: 理论上讲，美国梦宣称无论你来自何方，任何人都可以通过社会阶梯向上爬。

sentences.en: But today, it’s obvious that if your family’s wealthy, if you have a great education, if you grew up in a nice neighborhood, if you have some social connections, you can be successful.
sentences.zh: 但如今显而易见的是，如果你的家庭富有、受过良好教育、在一个不错的社区长大、拥有一定的社会人脉，你就能成功。

sentences.en: Social media has also changed the debate around the American Dream.
sentences.zh: 社交媒体也改变了围绕美国梦的争论。

sentences.en: Every day, you go onto Facebook or Instagram or TikTok and you see influencers or celebrities or wealthy content creators showing their luxury lifestyles online.
sentences.zh: 每天你打开Facebook、Instagram或TikTok，都会看到网红、名人或富有博主在网上展示他们的奢华生活方式。

sentences.en: There’s now a different standard for success.
sentences.zh: 现在有了一种不同的成功标准。

sentences.en: Many younger Americans, many younger people in the US, are less optimistic about the future.
sentences.zh: 许多年轻的美国人、美国许多年轻人对未来不那么乐观。

sentences.en: The American Dream seems to be dying in this case.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，美国梦似乎正在消亡。

sentences.en: But, despite all of these problems, the American Dream is still alive according to lots of people.
sentences.zh: 但是，尽管存在所有这些问题，在许多人看来，美国梦依然活着。

sentences.en: Or it’s not completely dead in any case.
sentences.zh: 或者说它无论如何都没有彻底消亡。

sentences.en: Every year, millions of people still move to the United States searching for better jobs and better opportunities.
sentences.zh: 每年仍有数百万为了寻找更好工作和更好机遇而移居美国。

sentences.en: It might be more difficult now, due to Trump’s immigration policies, but people still move to the US every single day.
sentences.zh: 由于特朗普的移民政策，现在可能更困难了，但人们仍然每天都在搬到美国。

sentences.en: I know people who have moved to the US relatively recently, and they have much higher paying jobs in the US than they would have had in the UK or in Japan or wherever they were living before.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些最近才搬到美国的人，他们在那里获得的薪水比他们在英国、日本或其他以前居住的地方要高得多。

sentences.en: Many immigrants to the US feel like the country is full of opportunity, especially compared to home countries.
sentences.zh: 许多美国移民觉得这个国家充满了机遇，尤其是与他们的祖国相比。

sentences.en: Salaries are higher. There’s more convenience in life.
sentences.zh: 薪水更高，生活更便利。

sentences.en: You can buy more things. It’s more expensive, but salaries are higher.
sentences.zh: 你可以买到更多东西。虽然消费更高，但薪水也更高。

sentences.en: So we have this kind of weird situation.
sentences.zh: 所以我们面临着这样一种奇怪的局面。

sentences.en: Many US citizens feel a little bit pessimistic about their future, but a lot of immigrants to the US remain optimistic about their opportunities.
sentences.zh: 许多美国公民对他们的未来感到有些悲观，但许多美国移民对他们的机遇依然保持乐观。

sentences.en: And it’s also true that the United States still produces remarkable success stories.
sentences.zh: 同样真实的是，美国依然不断创造出令人瞩目的成功故事。

sentences.en: There are entrepreneurs every day in the USA building billion-dollar companies.
sentences.zh: 美国每天都有企业家在创办价值数十亿美元的公司。

sentences.en: There are immigrants who were born into poverty and are now in the middle class.
sentences.zh: 有出生于贫困的移民现在跻身中产阶级。

sentences.en: There are athletes or artists or academics at universities or business owners who are achieving amazing success.
sentences.zh: 有运动员、艺术家、大学学者或企业主正在取得惊人的成功。

sentences.en: There are also systems in the US designed to create social mobility.
sentences.zh: 美国也有旨在创造社会流动性的体制。

sentences.en: Maybe not as good as other countries, but there are systems.
sentences.zh: 也许不如其他国家那么好，但体制确实存在。

sentences.en: Maybe the best way is to join the military.
sentences.zh: 也许最好的方法是参军。

sentences.en: If you join the military in the USA, you can use your military service as a pathway to university education and a stable job.
sentences.zh: 如果你在美国参军，你可以将你的服兵役经历作为通往大学教育和稳定工作的途径。

sentences.en: I know people who were active US soldiers or Air Force personnel, and they were studying master’s degrees or undergraduate degrees completely for free in the UK and in Japan because the military paid for it.
sentences.zh: 我认识一些曾担任美国陆军或空军现役人员的朋友，他们完全免费地在英国和日本攻读硕士或本科学位，因为军方支付了费用。

sentences.en: The US also has this startup culture and technology culture that has created a lot of opportunities, especially if you are in California or Austin, Texas, or New York.
sentences.zh: 美国还拥有这种创业文化和科技文化，创造了大量的机遇，特别是如果你身处加州、德克萨斯州奥斯汀或纽约。

sentences.en: Critics of the American Dream, people who say the American Dream is dead, will often compare today to the past: modern USA to what the USA looked like in the 1950s or’60s.
sentences.zh: 美国梦的批评者，也就是那些宣称美国梦已死的人，经常会把今天和过去做对比：用现代美国去对比20世纪50或60年代的美国。

sentences.en: But this might not be the best way to decide whether the American Dream is still alive.
sentences.zh: 但这可能并不是判断美国梦是否依然活着的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Perhaps if you compare the USA to the rest of the world, you get a different situation.
sentences.zh: 或许如果你把美国与世界其他地方进行对比，你会得出不同的情况。

sentences.en: Compared to countries where economic growth is weak, wages are low, there isn’t much freedom, the US still looks like a good option.
sentences.zh: 与那些经济增长疲软、工资低、缺乏自由的国家相比，美国仍然是一个不错的选择。

sentences.en: I guess the best way to say it is that the American Dream never really existed in the first place, at least this perfect American Dream.
sentences.zh: 我想最好的说法是，美国梦从一开始就从未真正存在过，至少这种完美的美国梦没有。

sentences.en: We have something called nostalgia. I introduced it in the vocabulary section.
sentences.zh: 我们有一种叫做“怀旧”的情绪。我在词汇部分介绍过它。

sentences.en: We look at the past and forget the negatives and only remember the positives.
sentences.zh: 我们回顾过去时会忘记负面因素，只记住积极因素。

sentences.en: So nostalgia simplifies history. The 1950s and’60s in the US were not perfect.
sentences.zh: 因此，怀旧情绪将历史简单化了。美国20世纪50和60年代并非完美无瑕。

sentences.en: I’m sure the people in the past were comparing their lives to people before them and thinking about what was different and whether it was better or not.
sentences.zh: 我确信过去的人们也曾将他们的生活与他们之前的人进行比较，思考着哪些地方不同，以及生活是否真的变得更好。

sentences.en: I guess, rather than dying, the American Dream is changing.
sentences.zh: 我想，美国梦与其说在消亡，不如说是在发生变化。

sentences.en: As I mentioned before, that traditional American Dream had a clear image.
sentences.zh: 正如我之前提到的，传统的美国梦有一个清晰的画面。

sentences.en: It was a house in the suburbs, a stable job, getting married, having children, buying a car, enough money to live comfortably.
sentences.zh: 那就是郊区的房子、稳定的工作、结婚、生子、买车、有足够的钱过上舒适的生活。

sentences.en: But younger people maybe define success a bit differently.
sentences.zh: 但年轻人对成功的定义可能会略有不同。

sentences.en: Maybe you define success as flexibility.
sentences.zh: 也许你将成功定义为灵活性。

sentences.en: Having a remote job or being a freelancer can be a bit more attractive now than staying in the same company for 30 years.
sentences.zh: 现在，拥有一份远程工作或成为自由职业者，可能比在同一家公司待上30年更具吸引力。

sentences.en: Some people like to think about their work-life balance rather than earning the highest possible salary.
sentences.zh: 有些人更喜欢考虑工作与生活的平衡，而不是追求尽可能的最高薪水。

sentences.en: Other people care more about their experiences.
sentences.zh: 另一些人则更在乎他们的经历。

sentences.en: They care more about travel or hobbies than owning a large house.
sentences.zh: 比起拥有大房子，他们更在乎旅行或爱好。

sentences.en: Of course, you could argue that this change is happening because those traditional goals, like homeownership, are too difficult for normal people.
sentences.zh: 当然，你可以辩称这种变化之所以发生，是因为那些传统目标（如拥有住房）对普通人来说太难实现了。

sentences.en: People may be adapting their dreams to economic reality.
sentences.zh: 人们可能正在使他们的梦想去适应经济现实。

sentences.en: People just accept the fact that it’s impossible to buy a house, or your rent is going to be really high, so you put your ambitions towards other goals, like your hobbies or being flexible.
sentences.zh: 人们只是接受了买不起房或者房租会非常高的现实，于是把抱负转向其他目标，比如培养爱好或追求灵活性。

sentences.en: So I thought it would be interesting to end this episode by looking at some other dreams.
sentences.zh: 因此我觉得，通过展望其他一些梦想来结束这期节目会很有趣。

sentences.en: The US is not the only place with a vision for success.
sentences.zh: 美国并不是唯一一个拥有成功愿景的地方。

sentences.en: It’s not the only place that immigrants want to move to.
sentences.zh: 它也不是唯一一个移民想要搬去的地方。

sentences.en: I know a lot of you guys, a lot of Thinking in English listeners, have ambitions to move to the UK or Australia or Canada or other places.
sentences.zh: 我知道你们中的很多人，《Thinking in English》的很多听众，都有搬到英国、澳大利亚、加拿大或其他地方的抱负。

sentences.en: For example, if there was a Canadian vision for success, it would probably be less focused on becoming rich, like in the US, more focused on safety or healthcare, education.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果存在一种加拿大的成功愿景，它可能不像美国那样专注于变得富有，而是更多地关注安全、医疗保健和教育。

sentences.en: Canada has a reputation for strong public services, even though housing costs there are very expensive and are a problem as well.
sentences.zh: 加拿大以强大的公共服务而闻名，尽管那里的房价也非常昂贵且同样是个问题。

sentences.en: Australia has a similar idea. There is an Australian dream.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚也有类似的理念。存在着所谓的“澳大利亚梦”。

sentences.en: I think a lot of British people want to move to Australia more than wanting to move to the US.
sentences.zh: 我想很多英国人比起搬去美国，更想搬去澳大利亚。

sentences.en: The Australian version of success is homeownership, middle-class comfort, a relaxed lifestyle, maybe living near the beach, nice weather.
sentences.zh: 澳大利亚版的成功是拥有住房、中产阶级的舒适生活、轻松的生活方式，也许是住在海滩附近、享受好天气。

sentences.en: This is what people think about when moving to Australia.
sentences.zh: 这就是人们在考虑搬到澳大利亚时所想的。

sentences.en: China has its own success narrative as well.
sentences.zh: 中国也有其自身的成功叙事。

sentences.en: Rapid economic growth over the past 30, 40, 50 years has changed China.
sentences.zh: 过去30、40、50年间的经济迅猛增长改变了中国。

sentences.en: Hundreds of millions of people used to be in poverty.
sentences.zh: 数亿人曾一度身处贫困。

sentences.en: Now they’re not. There are now huge opportunities for education and wealth in the country, and the Chinese government has even promoted the phrase the “Chinese Dream “, although it does tend to be a bit more on national success and collective progress
sentences.zh: 而现在他们不再贫困了。中国现在拥有巨大的教育和财富机遇，中国政府甚至还推广了“中国梦”这一说法，尽管它往往更偏向于国家成功和集体进步。

sentences.en: The UK, my country, is a little bit different, I think.
sentences.zh: 我的祖国英国则有些不同，我想。

sentences.en: Britain has traditionally had a stronger class system, so it’s been viewed as less socially mobile than the United States.
sentences.zh: 英国传统上拥有更森严的阶级制度，因此其社会流动性一直被认为不如美国。

sentences.en: In the US, everyone likes to define themselves as middle class, but in the UK ideas of self-improvement and financial success and moving up in life still exist.
sentences.zh: 在美国，每个人都喜欢把自己定义为中产阶级，但在英国，自我提升、经济成功以及生活向上的观念依然存在。

sentences.en: And then there are the Scandinavian countries, like Sweden and Norway and Denmark.
sentences.zh: 然后是斯堪的纳维亚国家，比如瑞典、挪威和丹麦。

sentences.en: Their models of success can look quite different from the version in the US.
sentences.zh: 他们的成功模式可能看起来与美国版本截然不同。

sentences.en: The focus is often on social security, work-life balance, having an overall good life.
sentences.zh: 其重点往往在于社会保障、工作与生活的平衡以及整体上过上美好的生活。

sentences.en: So the American Dream has traditionally focused on individual achievement, the idea that a person can individually rise through society with hard work and talent.
sentences.zh: 因此，美国梦传统上侧重于个人成就，即一个人可以通过努力工作和才华在社会中实现个人崛起。

sentences.en: But in other places, success might be defined a bit more collectively, might be creating a society where most people can live comfortably and securely.
sentences.zh: 但在其他地方，成功的定义可能更具集体性，可能是创造一个绝大多数人都能过上舒适和安全生活的社会。

sentences.en: Is the American Dream dead? For some people, I think inequality, expensive housing, debt, other things like this have made that traditional American Dream feel gone, dead, out of reach.
sentences.zh: 美国梦真的死了吗？对某些人来说，我认为不平等、昂贵的房价、债务以及其他诸如此类的事情让传统的美国梦感觉已经消逝、破灭、遥不可及。

sentences.en: For other people, the US still offers a lot of opportunities, especially compared to much of the world.
sentences.zh: 对另一些人来说，美国仍然提供了大量的机遇，尤其是与世界上大部分地区相比。

sentences.en: Some of my friends, who are highly skilled, have amazing jobs in the USA.
sentences.zh: 我的一些朋友技能娴熟，在美国拥有令人惊艳的工作。

sentences.en: Maybe it is the American Dream itself that’s changing.
sentences.zh: 也许发生变化的正是美国梦本身。

sentences.en: In the past, people dreamed of houses, cars, and jobs.
sentences.zh: 在过去，人们梦想的是房子、汽车和工作。

sentences.en: Today, people care more about freedom and flexibility and the quality of your life.
sentences.zh: 如今，人们更在乎自由、灵活性以及生活质量。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Do you think the American Dream still exists?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你认为美国梦依然存在吗？

sentences.en: Do you want to move to the US? Do you know anyone from your country who has moved to the US?
sentences.zh: 你想搬到美国吗？你认识来自你国家、搬去美国的人吗？

sentences.en: Has your generation been given fewer opportunities than previous generations?
sentences.zh: 你的这一代人获得的机遇是否比前几代人更少？

sentences.en: And does your country have its own version of a national dream?
sentences.zh: 你的国家有属于自己的国家梦想版本吗？
